name: Selected Topics in Databases and Information Systems
description:
Distributed systems form the foundation of many modern enterprise platforms, cloud services, and large-scale applications. Services such as Google Drive, Snowflake’s Data Platform, and Amazon S3 rely on distributed architectures to provide scalability, reliability, and availability. 

This course focuses on the design, specification, and validation of distributed data systems. Students will study the fault and communication models that shape the behavior of these systems, including partial failures, message delays, unreliable networks, replication, and concurrency. The course emphasizes how these assumptions influence system design and correctness. 

The course will teach students how to use formal specification techniques, such as TLA+, to model protocols and reason about important system properties such as safety, liveness, consistency, and fault tolerance. Students will also learn about practical validation techniques, including deterministic simulation testing and property-based testing, to uncover subtle bugs that arise in distributed environments.
prerequisites:
Grundlagen: Rechnernetze und Verteilte Systeme (IN0010) 
Introduction to Software Engineering (IN0006)
